prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues is a molecular design principle that changed what chemists and clinicians can do. A small molecule can now bring a target and an E3 ligase together and remove the protein rather than just occupy it. This reaches proteins that lack a conventional active site, and the design rules (ligand, linker, ternary-complex cooperativity) are chemical and transferable. Six of the eight opening ballots rank B068 in their top seven, three of them first, and it spans chemical biology, structural chemistry and drug discovery. The mechanism has been reproduced by many independent groups, and several degraders are in late-stage trials. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are what turned the original Crews-Deshaies peptide-based concept into drug-like, general chemistry, so the trio gives a concept-plus-enabling-chemistry story that can be explained in one citation.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved yet, so the clinical proof that justifies a Nobel-scale claim is still pending, and the prize could come a few years early. Three names also force a contestable cut: Sakamoto shares the original PROTAC paper, and Handa, Ito and Gray's cereblon and molecular-glue work is a distinct strand that a PROTAC-centred citation would sideline. A committee that cares about completeness may judge B068 too crowded to credit cleanly.

responses.point: Chabes also ranks B068 first, but proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa. He argues that Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains the glue mechanism, and he notes that Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray make the three-person cut contestable.
responses.response: I agree the cut is contestable and I take Handa's claim seriously, since cereblon is what made the glue mechanism chemically understandable. But I still prefer Ciulli, for two reasons. First, the citation then has one coherent subject, designed heterobifunctional degraders, and I do not have to bolt a separate molecular-glue story onto it. Second, Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are what made degraders general and drug-like. I would sooner leave glues and cereblon to a later prize than build a split citation that blurs the claim. I would reconsider if the committee wants a mechanism-first citation covering both strands.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks energy-landscape theory (B027) first as a mature, mechanism-level physical principle that is conceptually original and in no way redundant with the 2024 prize. He ranks B068 only fourth, partly because of the pending clinical validation.
responses.response: I share your preference for mature work with a clear mechanism, and B027 clearly meets that bar. I disagree on how much the missing approval counts. For a method that creates a new capability, the question is whether the capability is real, reproducible and broadly used, and that is answered: degraders are made routinely, mechanistically validated and carried by many groups. B027 is more mature, but most of its practical weight now sits in computational structure prediction, which the 2024 prize touched. B068 still changes what experimental chemists build. I do think B027 is a serious competitor and a good fallback if the committee decides a clinical approval is needed first.

responses.point: Linke ranks biomolecular phase separation (B022) first as the strongest bridge between thermodynamics and living matter, and places B068 sixth.
responses.response: The physical framing of condensates is attractive, but my reservation is chemical rather than conceptual. The consequence of B022 for chemistry is mainly a new way to describe cells, and your own uncertainty about whether in-vitro phase separation reflects true in-cell liquid-liquid phase separation points to a still-open question. For B068 the chemical consequence is a new class of molecules that can be designed and tested, with an unambiguous readout, which is the degradation of the target protein. I would find B022 more convincing once the in-cell relevance is settled, so I would keep it as a later candidate rather than a current one.

responses.point: Somfai puts B057, Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling, first because it is a general bond-forming method with lasting impact, and he ranks B068 last (eighth) among his choices.
responses.response: I agree B057 is mature, general and beyond doubt in impact. My difficulty is that it follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize closely, and you acknowledge that this overlap and the Kosugi/Migita precedent may reduce its novelty. B068 opens a new modality in chemical biology rather than refining a reaction class we have already honoured. Your general-method test also applies to B068: ligand and linker design rules are now applied across many targets and E3 ligases. I would not oppose B057 as a prize, but I would like to see the committee weigh novelty against the 2010 precedent explicitly.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize before any PROTAC is clinically approved.
Whether the three-name limit can be filled fairly between Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Sakamoto, Handa, Ito and Gray, and whether a molecular-glue strand should be included.

Whether the committee judges a second genome-editing or delivery prize (B026, B054) acceptable so soon after the 2020 CRISPR and 2023 mRNA recognitions; I rely on my own knowledge of clinical status, not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) and my Linkoping colleagues are not credited on any shortlisted ballot, and none of the shortlisted candidates is a close collaborator. I note only a loose thematic proximity of my biosensor and bioengineering work to nanoparticle and delivery topics such as B054.
